title: Maximum scan of one clause
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and $C$ a clause of natural-number-indexed literals. If $x$ is a concatenation of a prefix, the serialization of $C$, and a suffix, then for every counter length $n$, second-tape content, second-tape head position $b$, and output word $o$, there is a number of steps $t\le 2|\mathrm{enc}(C)|$ after which the machine is in state $2$ at the input position just after the serialized clause. Its counter length is the maximum of $n$ and the largest literal variable index in $C$ plus one (or $0$ if $C$ is empty); the counter head remains at $0$, and the second tape, its head, and the output are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: decomposition of $x$ as prefix, serialized clause, and suffix
replaced:
Let $C$ be a clause with serialization $\mathrm{ser}(C)$, and let $m_C$ be the
maximum of $v + 1$ over the literals $(v, b)$ of $C$ (or $0$ if $C$ is empty).
Suppose the input is $x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{ser}(C) \mathbin{+\!\!+} r$,
and the transducer is in its clause-level maximum state at input position $|p|$,
with counter length $n$, counter head at $0$, and arbitrary buffer, buffer head,
and output. Then there is a number $t \le 2\,|\mathrm{ser}(C)|$ of silent steps
after which the transducer is in formula-level maximum control at input position
$|p| + |\mathrm{ser}(C)|$, with counter length $\max(n, m_C)$, counter head back
at $0$, and buffer, buffer head, and output unchanged.
